newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney dismisses regional director - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney dismisses regional director - NYT.

text.p: Smith Barney Inc has dismissed its New England regional director, whose role in raising campaign cash for his brother's successful congressional campaign is under investigation, the New York Times said.
Robert Maloney was dismissed on Friday after he had been put on a leave of absence in the midst of the investigation, the Times said in its Tuesday editions.
Maloney's brother is Representative James Maloney, a Democrat from Connecticut who last year defeated Republican incumbent Gary Franks.

"Last Friday, Smith Barney terminated Mr. Maloney's employment with the firm," the company, which is part of the Travelers Group Inc, said. "Smith Barney will continue to cooperate fully with the federal authorities."
Neither Maloney nor his lawyer were available for comment.

Maloney helped raise money for his brother's campaigns, including $39,000 from 40 people at Smith Barney during his unsuccessful bid in 1994, the Times said. Last year, Smith Barney employees contributed $3,750 to Maloney's successful run for Congress.
